decisions.reason: The current complete paper collects new experimental data (national White-adult N737 and an additional current-study sample) and explicitly compares its observed negative-ad sponsor penalty in Results/Figure2a with Kahn and Geer1994. Its directly manipulated negative-versus-neutral advertisement and measured sponsor-minus-opponent evaluations empirically retest that attributed published penalty. A new racial-moderation theory and use of Brooks/Geer2007 stimulus presentation do not erase the published finding comparison; its own within-paper additional experiment is not the sole basis for classification. The recovered original publisher abstract verifies identity and empirical ad experiment, but lacks outcome details and full body; exact stimuli, penalty statistics and conditional components remain unverified, not invented. Those source-specific identity/outcome questions receive separate necessary review. Classification follows the actual new-data empirical relationship rather than the primary aim or a requirement to label the work a replication.
